mainTopic: Transferring an ox or slave only for its קנס, and קידושין involving a person who is half slave and half free.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: can someone give another person ownership of his ox only for goring, or of his slave only for שן ועין? The גמרא explains why the question is real both for רבי מאיר, since the קנס might never come about if the owner admits, and for the רבנן, since the ox and slave already exist. רבי אבא tries to prove from a ברייתא on ויליד ביתו that a slave can be worth nothing, which would not happen if every slave could be sold for his קנס. The גמרא answers that a טרפה slave who is also disgusting or covered with boils is truly worthless, so the proof does not decide the question. Next the גמרא asks whether a man who is half slave and half free can make קידושין with a free woman. A ברייתא about his 'heirs' is brought as proof, but רבא shows it only means heirs who would be entitled to the money in principle. Then comes a dispute about a woman who is half שפחה and half free. רבא and רב ששת say her קידושין fail, like betrothing half a woman, while רב חסדא argues nothing is held back, and רבה בר רב הונא publicly takes back his ruling. The amud ends as רב חסדא begins a case about such a woman betrothed to two brothers and יבום, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the question exists even for רבי מאיר: the owner might admit and be exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why even רבי מאיר might not allow this transfer: the penalty may never happen, because the owner can admit and be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will admit and become exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why the question is real even for רבי מאיר. The goring or eye-damage penalty may never actually be paid, because the owner can admit first and be exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allows transferring something not yet in the world when it will surely come into being, like fruit that will grow. A קנס, though, is not certain: someone who admits to a קנס before בית דין rules is exempt. So this case might be weaker than fruit, even for רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
Admits (in court, before witnesses come)
Becomes exempt
One who admits to a fine on his own is exempt from paying it (the rule assumed here)

phrases.english: Perhaps he will admit and become exempt.
phrases.notes: The penalty for goring or for knocking out a slave's tooth or eye is a קנס, and someone who admits to a קנס himself does not pay it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the argument from the previous part of the daf, which explained why רבי מאיר's view does not settle the question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption that רבי מאיר would clearly allow transferring an ox for goring or a slave for שן ועין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Unlike fruit that will surely grow, the קנס may never come about, because the owner can admit and be exempt.

steps.title: Why the question exists even for the רבנן: the ox and the slave already exist
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן forbid transferring something not yet in the world only when the object itself does not exist yet. Here the ox and slave are standing right there, so what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: And you can ask this question according to the רבנן too. The רבנן said a person cannot transfer something that has not come into the world only in a case like the fruit of a date palm, which does not exist at all right now. But here, the ox is standing here and the slave is standing here. So what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the question is open for the רבנן too. They might allow this transfer, because the ox and the slave already exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say you cannot transfer something not yet in the world. But maybe that only means things that don't exist at all, like fruit not yet grown. Here the ox and slave exist, and only the future penalty is missing, so the רבנן might agree. The step ends with the open question מאי.

keyTerms.meaning: And let the question be asked (the question applies here too)
They only said their ruling up to this point (limits a view to its own case)
Something that has not yet come into the world
Fruit of a date palm
It is standing right here (it already exists)

phrases.english: And you can ask this question according to the Rabbis too –
The Rabbis only said
that a person cannot transfer ownership of something
that has not come into the world –
in a case like the fruit of a date palm,
which, at least right now, do not exist;
but here – the ox is standing here
and the slave is standing here. What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing the question is open for רבי מאיר, the גמרא shows it is open for the רבנן too.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can someone transfer an ox only for goring, or a slave only for שן ועין, when the object exists but the penalty does not exist yet?

steps.title: רבי אבא brings a proof: why does the פסוק need to mention a slave born in the house?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes a ברייתא asking why the פסוק mentions a slave born in the כהן's house. If a bought slave eats תרומה, a home-born slave surely should!
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: Come and hear: "And one born in his house." Why does the פסוק need to say this? If a slave bought with money eats תרומה, then one born in the house surely does!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא starts a proof for the question by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא first asks why the פסוק needs the words ויליד ביתו at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a כהן's bought slave eats תרומה, and so does a slave born in his house. A slave born in the house belongs to the כהן even more fully, so a קל וחומר seems to make the second phrase unnecessary. The ברייתא's answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A slave born in the master's house
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
A slave acquired with money
Isn't it all the more so? (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said: Come and hear:
"And one born in his house" – why does the verse need to say this?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:11, about who in a כהן's household may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: If a slave bought with money eats,
then one born in the house – isn't it all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the open question מאי by bringing a ברייתא as a proof.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether one can transfer an ox for goring or a slave for שן ועין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining ויליד ביתו in ויקרא 22:11, about a כהן's slaves eating תרומה.

steps.title: The ברייתא's answer: a home-born slave eats even when he has no money value
steps.stepSummary: Without the extra words, we would think only a slave with money value eats תרומה. ויליד ביתו teaches that he eats in every case, even if he is worth nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק had not said it, I would have said: just as a bought slave has money value and eats, so too a home-born slave eats only if he has money value. How do we know he eats even when he is worth nothing? The פסוק says "one born in his house" to teach that he eats in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The words ויליד ביתו teach that a slave born in the house eats תרומה even when he is worth nothing, like a newborn baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר from the bought slave would carry over its limit: a bought slave was worth money. So we would think a home-born slave eats only if he has money value. The extra words remove that limit, and רבי אבא uses this point for the question in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: If it were so (if we only had the קל וחומר)
I would have said
Something with money value
In any case, no matter what

steps.whatToRemember: A slave born in a כהן's house eats תרומה even if he has no money value. The words ויליד ביתו teach this "מכל מקום", and רבי אבא brings it as his proof.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about תרומה, not about goring or שן ועין. The link to the question has not been explained yet. רבי אבא spells it out in step 7.

phrases.english: If so, I would have said:
phrases.notes: He means: if we only had the קל וחומר and no extra words in the פסוק.

phrases.english: Just as a slave bought with money,
who has money value, eats;
so too one born in the house,
only if he has money value, eats;

phrases.aramaic: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה כְּלוּם?
phrases.english: And how do we know that he eats even if he is worth nothing?
The verse says "one born in his house" – in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by answering why the פסוק needs the words ויליד ביתו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words teach that a home-born slave eats תרומה even when he has no money value, which the קל וחומר alone would not teach.

steps.title: The ברייתא raises another possible mistake
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a new possible mistake: maybe only a home-born slave eats even when worthless, while a bought slave eats only if he has money value.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I still might say: a slave born in the house eats תרומה whether or not he is worth money. But a slave bought with money eats only if he is worth money. If he is worth nothing, he does not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and raises a new challenge to itself. Now that we know a home-born slave eats even when worthless, maybe a bought slave still needs money value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 we learned that ויליד ביתו covers a slave who is worth nothing. Now the logic is flipped: maybe that rule is only for the home-born slave. A bought slave became the כהן's through money, so maybe he only counts while he has money value. This sets up the next step, where the פסוק answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: And I still might say: a phrase that raises a new possible mistake
A slave born in the master's house
A slave acquired by paying money
Worth money, having money value

phrases.english: And I still say:
one born in the house,
phrases.notes: He means a slave born in the כהן's house, from the פסוק in step 3.

phrases.english: whether he has money value,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף – אוֹכֵל;
phrases.english: or whether he has no money value, he eats;

phrases.aramaic: קִנְיַן כֶּסֶף, יֵשׁ בּוֹ שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף – אוֹכֵל,
phrases.english: one bought with money: if he has money value, he eats,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף – אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל;
phrases.english: if he has no money value, he does not eat;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 4's rule and suggests it might apply only to the home-born slave.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a worthless bought slave also eats תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bought slave comes through money, so maybe he counts only while he is worth money.

steps.title: The פסוק puts both slaves together
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק lists the bought slave and the home-born slave side by side. So just as a worthless home-born slave eats, a worthless bought slave eats too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'one bought with his money and one born in his house.' Just as the home-born slave eats even if he is worth nothing, so too the bought slave eats even if he is worth nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own challenge from the פסוק. It compares the two kinds of slaves, which shows that a bought slave eats even when he is worth nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names both slaves together, so they follow the same rule. The rule from step 4 (worthless still eats) now carries over to the bought slave. The key fact for רבי אבא's proof is now clear: a slave can exist who is worth nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches: brings the answer from the פסוק
Just as ... so too: compares two cases
He is worth nothing at all

steps.whatToRemember: This ברייתא shows that a slave can have zero value. רבי אבא is about to use exactly this point.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"The purchase of his money and one born in his house"
just as one born in the house,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה כְּלוּם – אוֹכֵל;
phrases.english: even though he is worth nothing, eats;
so too the purchase of his money,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה כְּלוּם – אוֹכֵל.
phrases.english: even though he is worth nothing, eats.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: קִנְיַן כַּסְפּוֹ וִילִיד בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by comparing the two slaves.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a worthless bought slave eat תרומה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The פסוק compares him to the home-born slave, who eats even when worth nothing.

steps.title: רבי אבא's proof: every slave would have some value
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא argues that if a slave could be sold for the קנס, every slave would be worth something. But the ברייתא speaks of a worthless slave, so a sale for the קנס must not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think a slave whose master sold him just for the קנס is really sold, is there any slave who could not be sold for the קנס?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא now uses the ברייתא as a proof. He argues that selling a slave just for his קנס must not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If selling the right to the קנס counted as a real sale, every slave would always have some value: the קנס. Then no slave could ever be 'worth nothing,' as the ברייתא says. So the ברייתא suggests that a sale for the קנס is not a real sale.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would think: opens a proof by showing what goes wrong
A fixed fine, here the thirty שקלים paid when an ox kills a slave
Can be sold

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that a slave whose master sold him for the penalty is sold,
phrases.notes: This is the question from the earlier steps: can a master sell only the right to the fine?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִיכָּא עַבְדָּא דְּלָא מִזְדַּבַּן לִקְנָסָא?!
phrases.english: is there any slave who cannot be sold for the penalty?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 6 to answer the question of step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a slave sold only for the קנס is not really sold
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא saying a slave can be worth nothing

steps.title: A טרפה slave has no קנס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is a slave who cannot be sold for the קנס: a טרפה slave. So the ברייתא could be talking about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, there is such a slave: a slave who is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אבא's proof. There is a slave with no קנס value: a טרפה, who is going to die anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a slave is a טרפה, an ox that kills him does not pay the קנס. So even if a sale for the קנס works, a טרפה slave would still be worth nothing. The ברייתא can be about him, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
A slave with a deadly injury who will die soon

phrases.english: Yes, there is: a slave who is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 7's proof by finding a slave with no קנס value.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A טרפה slave has no קנס value, so the ברייתא could be about him.

steps.title: But he can still stand before his master
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even a טרפה slave can stand before his master to honor him, so he is worth something.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is fit to stand before his master!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 8. Even a טרפה slave has some use, so he is not 'worth nothing.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing before the master to honor him is a real service. A slave who can do it has some value. So the טרפה case does not give us a fully worthless slave.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so: introduces a challenge
To stand before him, to serve and honor the master

phrases.english: But he is fit to stand before him!
phrases.notes: Him means his master. Standing before him honors the master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 8's טרפה answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a טרפה slave is worth nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He can still serve by standing before his master, so he has value.

steps.title: A disgusting slave or one covered with boils
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a טרפה slave who is also disgusting or covered with boils, so he cannot even stand before his master.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a slave who is disgusting or covered with boils.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the טרפה answer. The slave is also so repulsive that standing before his master would bring no honor, so he really is worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding these details removes the last bit of value the slave had. Now a slave can be worthless even if a sale for the קנס works. So רבי אבא's proof does not decide the question, and the question stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: Disgusting, repulsive
Covered with boils

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבא's proof is turned back. A worthless slave can exist anyway, so whether a sale for the קנס works stays an open question.

phrases.english: With one who is disgusting or afflicted with boils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by narrowing the case of the טרפה slave.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טרפה slave still has value because he can stand before his master.
steps.terutzMaskana: A טרפה slave who is also disgusting or covered with boils has no value at all.

steps.title: קידושין by a man who is half slave and half free
steps.stepSummary: A new question: what happens when a man who is half slave and half free makes קידושין with a free woman?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: a man who is half slave and half free made קידושין with a free woman. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with an איבעיא. It asks whether the קידושין of a half-slave, half-free man works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A free woman may marry a free Jewish man, but she cannot marry a slave. This man is both at once. So it is unclear whether his קידושין take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked of them, meaning of the חכמים
Half slave and half free
Made קידושין, betrothed
A free woman

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין,
phrases.english: one who is half slave and half free,
who betrothed a free woman, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the קנס discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the קידושין of a half-slave, half-free man with a free woman take effect?

steps.title: Why the question is not simple
steps.stepSummary: Even if 'be betrothed to half of me' works for a free man, that may be because she could marry all of him. She cannot marry all of a half-slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say that when a Jewish man tells a Jewish woman 'Be betrothed to half of me,' she is betrothed, that is because she is fit for all of him. Here she is not fit for all of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is hard. A case that looks similar may not really be the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a free man offers half of himself, the קידושין can work because she is allowed to marry the whole man. With a half-slave, the slave half is a man she may never marry. So the earlier rule may not carry over, and the question stays open for now.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: even if we accept one side, this case may still differ
Be betrothed to half of me
She is fit for all of him

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an answer. The גמרא is only showing why the half-slave case may differ from the half-of-me case, so the question is still open.

phrases.english: If you say:
"A Jewish man who said to a Jewish woman:
'Be betrothed to half of me,' she is betrothed"
that is because she is fit for all of him;
here, she is not fit for all of him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the question in step 11 is hard.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the rule of 'be betrothed to half of me' be applied to a half-slave?

steps.title: Maybe the half-slave case is even better than half a woman
steps.stepSummary: Even if betrothing half a woman fails, that is because the man left part of her out. The half-slave leaves nothing out, so what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that a Jewish man who betroths half a woman does not make a valid קידושין, that is because he held back part of his acquisition. But this slave did not hold back anything. So what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around and shows why the half-slave case might still work. Then it asks again: what is the law?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a free man betroths 'half a woman,' it fails because his קידושין does not cover all of her. The half-slave is different. His free half betroths her completely, so nothing of her is left out. This gives a reason to think it could work, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (if you decide that way)
Half a woman
Left over, held back
His acquisition

phrases.english: And if you say
that a Jewish man who betroths half a woman
she is not betrothed
that is because he left part of her out of his acquisition
but this slave did not leave anything out of his acquisition
What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 12 gave a reason the half-slave's קידושין might fail. This step gives the opposite reason, that it might work, and repeats the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the קידושין of a half-slave to a free woman valid?

steps.title: Proof from the ox that killed a half-slave
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says half the כופר goes to the half-slave's heirs. If he could not marry, how would he have heirs?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if an ox killed a man who is half slave and half free, the owner gives half the קנס to his master and half the כופר to his heirs. If you say his קידושין is not valid, where would he get heirs from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. The ברייתא mentions the half-slave's heirs, which suggests he can marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an ox kills a slave, the owner pays a fixed קנס to the master. When it kills a free person, he pays כופר to the heirs. A half-slave gets half of each. Heirs usually means children, and children come from marriage. So it seems his קידושין works.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed fine (thirty שקלים for a slave killed by an ox)
Ransom money paid when an ox kills a free person
His heirs

phrases.english: Come and hear
If [an ox] killed one who is half slave
phrases.notes: The word 'ox' is not written. The קנס and כופר mentioned next are what an ox's owner pays when his ox kills someone.

phrases.english: and half free
he gives half the fine to his master
and half the ransom to his heirs
And if you say
his betrothal is not a valid betrothal
where does he have heirs from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from step 13 using a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a half-slave's קידושין is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא saying half the כופר goes to the half-slave's heirs

steps.title: The ox only made him a טרפה, and 'heirs' means himself
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says the ox did not kill him but made him a טרפה. 'His heirs' really means the half-slave himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: the case is where the ox made him a טרפה. And what does 'his heirs' mean? Himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה pushes back on the proof. He says the man is still alive, so the money goes to him and not to any children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the victim is alive as a טרפה, no heirs are needed, because he takes the money himself. Then the ברייתא says nothing about whether he can marry.

keyTerms.meaning: Fatally injured; considered as good as dead
Himself

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said
It is a case where it made him a tereifa
phrases.notes: The ox did not kill him outright. It wounded him fatally.

phrases.english: And what is 'his heirs'? Himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה כְּשֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ טְרֵפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 14 by reading the case differently.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be about a living טרפה, so 'heirs' could mean the victim himself.

steps.title: רבא's two problems with the טרפה reading
steps.stepSummary: רבא says 'heirs' cannot mean the man himself, and כופר is only paid after death anyway, according to ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: there are two refutations of this. One: the ברייתא says 'his heirs.' And another: this is כופר, and ריש לקיש said כופר is paid only after death!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב אדא בר אהבה's answer with two separate problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, nobody calls a living man his own 'heirs,' so that reading does not fit the words. Second, ריש לקיש rules that כופר is paid only after death, so a living טרפה would not get כופר at all. The טרפה answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: There are two refutations of this
It teaches (the wording says)

phrases.english: Rava said
There are two refutations of this
One: it teaches 'his heirs'
And furthermore, it is ransom
and Reish Lakish said

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹפֶר אֵין מִשְׁתַּלֵּם אֶלָּא לְאַחַר מִיתָה!
phrases.english: Ransom is paid only after death!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the deflection in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's טרפה reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'heirs' does not fit a living man, and כופר is not paid while the victim is alive.

steps.title: Heirs who are fit to take, but do not exist
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'his heirs' means heirs would be fit to take the כופר, but the half-slave really has none. So there is no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: they are fit to take it, but he has none.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own way to reject the proof. The ברייתא only says who would be entitled to the money in principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not saying the half-slave actually has children. It is saying that his half of the כופר is the kind of money heirs would get, but in this case there are none. So the ברייתא does not show that his קידושין works, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to take (entitled in principle)
But he does not have (any)

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the ox ברייתא falls away. 'His heirs' only means heirs would be entitled in principle, so the half-slave's קידושין is still an open question.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said
It is fit for heirs to take it, but he does not have any.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא רָאוּי לִיטּוֹל וְאֵין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After knocking down רב אדא בר אהבה's answer, רבא gives a better way to reject the proof from step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא that a half-slave can have heirs
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'His heirs' describes who would be entitled to the money in principle, not heirs who actually exist.

steps.title: רבא: A half-maidservant cannot be betrothed
steps.stepSummary: רבא compares a half-שפחה half-בת חורין to the case of betrothing half a woman, and rules that her קידושין are not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Just as a man who betroths half a woman does not make her betrothed, so too, a woman who is half maidservant and half free who was betrothed: her betrothal is not a betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic, a woman who is half slave and half free. רבא rules that her קידושין do not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא uses a known rule as his model: if a man says 'half of you is betrothed to me,' nothing happens. Since only half of this woman is free, he treats any קידושין to her as reaching only half a woman, so they fail.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is half maidservant and half free (one of two owners freed his half)
One who betroths half a woman
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַמְקַדֵּשׁ חֲצִי אִשָּׁה – אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: Just as one who betroths half a woman – she is not betrothed,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ חֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין
phrases.english: so too, one who is half maidservant and half free woman
who was betrothed – her betrothal is not a betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַמְקַדֵּשׁ חֲצִי אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the half-slave man (steps 13-17) to the half-slave woman, using the same 'half a woman' comparison raised in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A half-maidservant half-free woman cannot receive valid קידושין, just like betrothing half a woman.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא teaches the same ruling in public
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא publicly teaches the same rule as רבא: a half-שפחה who was betrothed is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא taught in public: Just as one who betroths half a woman does not make her betrothed, so too, a half-maidservant half-free woman who was betrothed is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא gives a public lecture with the same ruling as רבא. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the law here. The point is that this ruling was now taught publicly. That makes it a big deal when he later takes it back.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught publicly, gave a public lecture

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna taught publicly:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַמְקַדֵּשׁ חֲצִי אִשָּׁה – אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: Just as one who betroths half a woman – she is not betrothed,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ חֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין
phrases.english: so too, one who is half maidservant and half free woman
who was betrothed – she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats רבא's ruling as a public teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same as רבא: the half-maidservant's קידושין do not take effect.

steps.title: רב חסדא: The two cases are not alike
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא challenges the comparison. Betrothing half a woman leaves part of her out, but here the man takes all that can be taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: Are these cases comparable? There, he left part of her out of his acquisition. Here, he did not leave anything out of his acquisition!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks the comparison that רבא and רבה בר רב הונא built their ruling on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In 'half a woman,' the man chose to take only half when he could have taken all of her, so the קידושין fail. With a half-free woman, he takes the entire free part. Nothing that could be betrothed is left out, so the reason for failure does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they alike? (a challenge to a comparison)
He left over, held back
Acquisition
There... here (contrasting two cases)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: מִי דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to him: Are they comparable?
There, he left part out of his acquisition,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the man who betroths half a woman. He could have taken all of her but only took half.

phrases.english: here, he did not leave anything out of his acquisition!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison used in steps 18-19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between a half-free woman and betrothing half a woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason 'half a woman' fails is that the man held back part of what he could take. Here nothing is held back, so the comparison breaks down.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא publicly takes back his ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא calls an אמורא, admits his mistake with a פסוק about stumbling, and now rules that the half-שפחה's קידושין are valid, using רב חסדא's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא then set up a speaker for himself and taught: 'And let this stumbling-block be under your hand' – a person does not truly understand תורה unless he first stumbles in it. Although they said that one who betroths half a woman does not make her betrothed, a half-maidservant half-free woman who was betrothed is betrothed. What is the reason? There, he left part out of his acquisition; here, he did not leave anything out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא accepts רב חסדא's challenge. He publicly announces that he was wrong and reverses his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He brings a פסוק to teach that making mistakes is part of learning Torah. His new ruling is that her קידושין are valid. His reason is רב חסדא's point: unlike 'half a woman,' nothing here is held back.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the speaker who announces the teacher's words aloud to the crowd
Stumbling-block
Stumbles, makes a mistake
What is the reason?

steps.whyThisMatters: A great teacher publicly admits his error. The lesson is that admitting a mistake is part of reaching the truth of Torah.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אוֹקֵים רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna went back and set up a speaker for himself,
and taught: 'And let this stumbling-block be under your hand' –

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: a person does not understand words of Torah,
unless he stumbles in them;

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ הַמְקַדֵּשׁ חֲצִי אִשָּׁה – אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: although they said that one who betroths half a woman – she is not betrothed,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין שֶׁנִּתְקַדְּשָׁה –
phrases.english: but a half-maidservant half-free woman who was betrothed –
her betrothal is a valid betrothal.
What is the reason?
There, he left part out of his acquisition,
here, he did not leave anything out of his acquisition.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אוֹקֵים רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רב חסדא's objection and reverses the ruling of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Revised view: a half-maidservant half-free woman can receive valid קידושין, because nothing is held back.

steps.title: רב ששת defends the original ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת restates רבא's original view: a half-שפחה's קידושין are not valid, just like betrothing half a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Just as one who betroths half a woman does not make her betrothed, so too, a half-maidservant half-free woman who was betrothed: her betrothal is not a betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת takes the side of the original ruling, against the retraction. He goes on to defend it against a source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after רב חסדא's point, רב ששת holds that the comparison to 'half a woman' stands. So the dispute is now open: רבא and רב ששת say invalid, while רב חסדא and the revised רבה בר רב הונא say valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too (a comparison formula)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַמְקַדֵּשׁ חֲצִי אִשָּׁה – אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: Just as one who betroths half a woman – she is not betrothed,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ חֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין
phrases.english: so too, one who is half maidservant and half free woman
who was betrothed – her betrothal is not a betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַמְקַדֵּשׁ חֲצִי אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבא's ruling (step 18) against the retraction in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The half-maidservant's קידושין are not valid.

steps.title: A source that seems to show she can be betrothed
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת raises a possible challenge himself: a ברייתא defines שפחה חרופה as a half-free woman betrothed to an עבד עברי, which implies she can be betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if someone whispers to you, saying: Who is the 'designated maidservant'? This is one who is half maidservant and half free, betrothed to a Hebrew slave. So it seems she can be betrothed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת predicts that someone will challenge his ruling from a ברייתא. He states that challenge here and answers it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls the half-free woman 'betrothed' to an עבד עברי. If her קידושין never work, how could she be called betrothed? That would go against רב ששת's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Whispers to you (suggests to you)
The 'designated maidservant' in the תורה
A Jewish slave
Apparently, this shows that
Able to be betrothed

phrases.english: And if a person whispers to you, saying:
Who is a designated maidservant? –

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ שֶׁחֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין
phrases.english: This is one who is half maidservant and half free woman
who is betrothed to a Hebrew slave;
apparently she is able to be betrothed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An expected objection to רב ששת's ruling in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that a half-maidservant cannot be betrothed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes her as betrothed to an עבד עברי, which implies her קידושין can work.

steps.title: Answer: Follow רבי ישמעאל's reading
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that רבי ישמעאל explains שפחה חרופה as a full כנענית maidservant betrothed to an עבד עברי, so that source does not have to be about a half-free woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say to him: Go to רבי ישמעאל, who says it is a Canaanite maidservant betrothed to a Hebrew slave.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת deflects the challenge. There is another view of what שפחה חרופה means, and it does not involve a half-free woman at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that mentions a half-free woman is only one opinion. רבי ישמעאל reads the case as a full שפחה כנענית, so his view gives no proof that a half-free woman can be betrothed. רב ששת sides with רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Go over to (follow the view of)
A non-Jewish maidservant owned fully by a Jew

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute stays open. רבא and רב ששת say a half-maidservant cannot be betrothed, like 'half a woman.' רב חסדא and the revised רבה בר רב הונא say she can, because nothing is held back.

phrases.aramaic: אֱמוֹר לוֹ: כְּלָךְ אֵצֶל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: Say to him: Go over to Rabbi Yishmael,
for he says –
it is about a Canaanite maidservant betrothed to a Hebrew slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֱמוֹר לוֹ: כְּלָךְ אֵצֶל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the challenging source to one opinion and adopts another תנא's reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that a half-free woman can be betrothed.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי ישמעאל, שפחה חרופה is a full כנענית maidservant, so there is no proof against רב ששת.

steps.title: Can a full Canaanite maidservant even be betrothed?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת questions his own answer: a שפחה כנענית cannot receive קידושין, so how could רבי ישמעאל call her 'betrothed'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is a Canaanite maidservant someone who can be betrothed?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks the answer he just gave in step 24. He points out that a full שפחה כנענית cannot receive קידושין at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, רב ששת said that רבי ישמעאל reads שפחה חרופה as a full שפחה כנענית who is 'מאורסת' (betrothed) to an עבד עברי. But a full שפחה כנענית cannot be betrothed, so the word 'מאורסת' cannot mean real קידושין for her. This forces a new reading of that word.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish maidservant owned by a Jew
Someone who can be betrothed, someone who can receive קידושין

phrases.english: But is a Canaanite maidservant someone who can be betrothed?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי ישמעאל's view that רב ששת cited in step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'מאורסת' in רבי ישמעאל's definition of שפחה חרופה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full שפחה כנענית cannot receive קידושין, so calling her 'מאורסת' cannot be literal

steps.title: Betrothed really means designated
steps.stepSummary: In רבי ישמעאל's words, 'מאורסת' must mean 'designated' (מיוחדת). The ברייתא can be read the same way, so it does not prove that a half-שפחה can be betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? What does 'betrothed' mean? Designated. Here too, what does 'betrothed' mean? Designated.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers his own question. Since 'מאורסת' must mean 'designated' for רבי ישמעאל, the same meaning can be applied in the ברייתא from step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We are forced to read 'מאורסת' as מיוחדת (set aside for him) in רבי ישמעאל's statement. Once we know the word can carry that meaning, the ברייתא about the half-free woman can mean the same thing. So the ברייתא no longer proves that a half-שפחה can receive real קידושין, and רב ששת's ruling from step 22 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, what must you say?' This shows that one explanation is forced, and the same explanation can then be used elsewhere
Betrothed
Designated, set aside for a particular man, without real קידושין
Here too, the same applies in this case

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'מאורסת' in these sources can mean 'designated' rather than truly betrothed. So no source here proves that a half-שפחה can receive קידושין, and רב ששת's ruling, the same as רבא's, holds.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב ששת gave up his position. He questioned his own answer only to reach a stronger one: both sources use 'מאורסת' to mean 'designated,' and that defends his view.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
What does 'betrothed' mean? Designated.
Here too, what does 'betrothed' mean? Designated.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the ברייתא about the half-free woman from step 23.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 and uses that answer to close the challenge from step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word (מאורסת = מיוחדת), then applying the same reading to the challenging source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls a half-free woman 'מאורסת' to an עבד עברי, which suggests real קידושין
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מאורסת' means designated, so the ברייתא does not prove that a half-שפחה's קידושין work

steps.title: רב חסדא's case: a half-שפחה betrothed to two brothers
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a half-שפחה betrothed to ראובן, who is then freed and betrothed to שמעון, may do יבום with לוי after both brothers die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A woman who is half maidservant and half free was betrothed to ראובן. Then she was freed, and she was betrothed again, to שמעון. If both of them died, she goes to יבום with לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא opens a new ruling about a half-שפחה who received קידושין from two brothers, one before she was freed and one after. His statement continues past this point, where his reason is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case makes us ask how two sets of קידושין from two brothers, one made while she was half-slave and one after she was freed, affect יבום after both die. רב חסדא rules that she does go to יבום with the third brother, לוי. His reason, which shows how he views the first קידושין, comes in the next text.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is half maidservant and half free
She was freed (set free completely)
She goes to יבום, marrying the brother of her dead husband

steps.whyThisMatters: This case tests what the earlier debate about a half-שפחה's קידושין means in practice for יבום.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A woman who is half maidservant and half free
who was betrothed to Reuven, and was then freed,
and then was betrothed again, to Shimon,
phrases.notes: ראובן, שמעון and לוי are understood to be brothers. That is why יבום comes up at all.

phrases.english: and both of them died,
she goes to levirate marriage with Levi,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא חֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the debate about whether a half-שפחה's קידושין work, the גמרא turns to a new ruling from רב חסדא about יבום for such a woman
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A half-שפחה betrothed to ראובן, then freed and betrothed to שמעון, goes to יבום with לוי after both brothers die. The reason continues in the next text.
